delivered: An independent token-replay workbench is available from the landing page and both event-log and object-centric toolbars without requiring a discovered model or cached source.
Original CSV/TSV/XES/gzip-XES uploads and supplied PNML files are retained, hashed, and downloadable alongside the exact completed request and native response.

Forward replay exposes the native complete typed public carrier, place/transition/unknown-activity fitness maps, variant grouping, returned names/labels, hidden-path caches and native replay policies.
Backwards replay exposes its native complete trace diagnostics. The forward public carrier and PLTR maps remain explicitly unavailable for backwards requests; unsupported combinations return errors.
Log, stream, dataframe and lazyframe inputs are selectable. Flat CSV inputs use original parser rows and columns; native case grouping and ordering remain distinct from already grouped logs.
A native EventDataView and flat-input full-forward replay entry point delegates through the existing native projection, grouping and hard event caps without changing the replay algorithms.
The shared CSV reader preserves quoted LF/CRLF fields, escaped quotes, source row positions and timestamp-sorted grouped logs. Unterminated quoted fields retain an explicit native error.
Header-only CSV inputs resolve their declared activity column, including custom and aliased names, and accept exact zero-event caps in every native input shape and both directions.

Inspection and CSV exports retain every trace, per-event diagnostic, model ID, supplied marking and zero-key membership, typed public value/object key/float hex, and integer token beyond uint64. Paging and selected-row JSON retain complete values.
boundaries: Feature delivery only. No package or module parity status or selector list is promoted; all 228 incomplete catalogue units remain in scope.

Existing native forward/backwards algorithms, full-carrier grouping, fitting classification, ordering and hidden-search bounds are retained. Broader reference algorithm, solver, numeric and scalability parity remains open.
The full public tagged carrier and PLTR maps are native forward capabilities. Backwards returns native trace diagnostics and no fabricated forward carrier.

CSV flat shapes retain original native parser tables. XES flat shapes are native conversions of the imported grouped log; arbitrary external dataframe objects, dtypes/index/categorical identity and schema behavior remain separate parity gates.

Ordinary trace JSON shares the existing native numeric serializer; the forward tagged public carrier retains exact float hex. This checkpoint does not certify all ordinary JSON float formatting against the reference.

Native direct-API metadata controls, full diagnostic/root-cause/duration contracts, marked-net semantics, callbacks, parameter defaults/errors and remaining replay/alignment workflows still require complete catalogue review.
All strict Unicode, type, ordering, marking, concurrency, performance and integration requirements remain in scope.
